newsitem.title: USA: U.S. officials to conduct TWA fuel tank tests.
newsitem.headline: U.S. officials to conduct TWA fuel tank tests.

text.p: U.S. officials investigating last summer's explosion of TWA Flight 800 said on Wednesday they would start tests soon on "fuel cross-feeding" as part of the probe into the crash that killed all 230 people on board.

National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) officials said they wanted to see if drawing fuel from a wing tank through a partially full centre tank to engines on the opposite side of the plane could cause static electricity and an explosion.

Last month the board said the wreckage of the Trans World Airlines Inc. jet was consistent with a centre fuel tank explosion that could have been caused by vapours inside the partially full tank rising to flash point temperatures.

But it has not yet determined the cause of the crash -- whether it was mechanical failure or a bomb. The Paris-bound Boeing Co. 747 exploded shortly after takeoff from New York's Kennedy Airport on July 17. Most of its wreckage has been recovered fom the ocean bottom off Long Island.

Board officials said the cockpit tape recorder picked up a comment by the pilot just before the crash that he would begin cross-feeding, but if was not known if he actually did. The tests would replicate the movement of fuel from a wing fuel tank through piping to the centre tank to assess the effect of mixing fuel and vapours and see how the combination might cause a temperature rise, the officials said.

Last month the board recommended that the Federal Aviation Administration order plane-makers to take steps to assure that fuel-air mixtures do not reach flash point temperatures. Their recommendations included insulating fuel tanks from outside heat sources and installing gauges to monitor fuel tank temperatures.
The FAA said it was studying the recommendations and would take action as warranted.
